title: Chunked assembly and KV-pin heuristics for streaming chat micro-batches
creator: Priya Desai
description: Design and implement a batch formation heuristic tailored for streaming chat completions that minimizes end-to-end latency while keeping GPU KV cache pressure and memory fragmentation under control. The goal is a robust micro-batching strategy that: 1) groups token-generation work into short-lived micro-batches (“chunks”) to retain low tail latency for interleaved interactive sessions, 2) pins hot KV pages for active sessions to avoid eviction thrashing, and 3) negotiates GPU slab reservations for long-lived contexts to reduce costly host-device transfers.
decisions: Adopt a chunked-assembly approach instead of waiting for fixed time windows: flush micro-batches once token count or deadline budget is reached.
Introduce a KV pinning TTL per session (default 3s) that is refreshed on active generation and decays for idle contexts.
Allocate a small hot-region slab per GPU (configurable) that stores pinned KV pages; fallback to host staging for cold evictions.
Use deadline-driven preemption: if a high-priority interactive request arrives, preempt low-priority queued chunks rather than the pinned KV heap.
Expose config knobs (chunk_max_tokens, chunk_deadline_ms, kv_pin_ttl_ms, slab_reserve_mb) in runtime config and Console.
Do not change on-disk model layout; kernel selection unchanged. This is a scheduling/allocator-level change only.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 - Priya: Initial spike — sketched chunk-flush state machine and KV pin TTL semantics. Recorded trade-offs in design doc (link below).
2026-03-02 - Liam: Implemented prototype in in-memory scheduler branch 'chunk-assembly/v1'. Added unit tests for chunk timeouts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4312

2026-03-04 - Priya: Runner benchmark against streaming baseline. Observed median latency +5ms, p95 improved by 12% under 60 concurrent sessions. GPU memory steady state reduced host↔device transfers by 28% in the microbenchmark.

acceptance_criteria: New heuristic implemented behind runtime feature flag 'chunk_assembly_v1'.
End-to-end p95 latency for 1-2s chat completions is no worse than baseline +15% under 200 concurrent sessions, target: <= baseline +8%.
Host↔GPU KV transfers reduced in steady-state by >=20% compared to baseline in the microbenchmark ensemble.
No increase in OOM incidents on canary fleets after applying adaptive slab grow/shrink for 72 hours.
Console exposes knobs and a heatmap for pinned-KV; documentation and runbook updated.
testing_plan: Unit tests for chunk flush conditions (token threshold, deadline expiry, high-priority preemption).
Integration test harness that replays 10k streaming sessions with mixed lengths and priorities to validate KV pin TTL behavior.
Canary rollout on dedicated cluster (canary-3) for 2 weeks with traffic ramp and anomaly detection rules.
Chaos test: simulate GPU eviction and host-device bandwidth pressure to ensure graceful degradation and fallbacks.
benchmarks: Baseline: streaming scheduler (no chunking) - p50=48ms p95=342ms under 120 concurrent sessions (toy model, seq mean=48 tokens).
Prototype chunk-assembly v1 - p50=53ms p95=300ms under same load; KV host transfer reduction 28%.
Adaptive slab reserve experiment - reduced p95 variance by 18% on long-tail sessions (>8s).
notes: Trade-offs: More aggressive pinning reduces host-device thrash but increases slab fragmentation; adaptive shrink/grow heuristics are required to avoid starving other contexts.
Edge-case: very long-running completions (>60s) must be spooled to host-backed KV regions after configurable grace period to avoid unbounded slab residency.
Operational visibility: heatmap must show per-session pinned bytes and pin refresh rate to diagnose hotspots.
